marking_schemes.question_text: What are biodegradable wastes? How are these biodegradable wastes helpful?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Wastes which can be decomposed into simpler substances by micro-organisms like bacteria. Usefulness: used as biofertilisers (nutrient-rich, non-polluting, cheap) / enrich soil / no soil pollution / maintain soil texture / eco-friendly / reduce landfill / increase humus.
key_points: Wastes decomposed into simpler substances by micro-organisms
Useful as manure / biofertiliser, enriching soil and reducing landfill waste
marking_schemes.model_answer: Biodegradable wastes are wastes that can be broken down into simpler substances by micro-organisms such as bacteria. They are helpful because they can be composted into nutrient-rich manure that enriches the soil without pollution.

marking_schemes.question_text: The vehicular traffic is a major problem in metro cities. Write two ways in which traffic congestion affects environment. Suggest three methods to reduce traffic on roads.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Effects: air pollution / greenhouse emissions concentrated at a place / secondary pollutants / noise pollution / depletion of fossil fuels / acid rain, ozone depletion, smog. (Any two) Methods: mass or public transport and car pools / expressways / road maintenance / ease bottlenecks / fines for breaking rules / staggered office hours and work from home / good signals / odd-even scheme / separate lanes / digital tolls / time restriction on heavy vehicles / one-way roads. (Any three)
key_points: Two environmental effects of congestion: air pollution; noise pollution; greenhouse emissions; smog; fuel depletion
Three methods to reduce traffic: public transport / car pools; staggered hours / work from home; odd-even scheme; separate lanes; better roads and signals
marking_schemes.model_answer: Traffic congestion causes air pollution as idling vehicles emit exhaust, and noise pollution from honking and engines. Traffic can be reduced by encouraging public transport and car pools, staggering office hours or allowing work from home, and using an odd-even vehicle scheme on alternate days.
common_errors: Wrote the same points for both parts

marking_schemes.question_text: Sanitary land fill and Incineration are two methods of waste disposal. Briefly describe the two processes. Suggest any other ecofriendly method of waste disposal for biodegradable wastes.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sanitary landfills are sites where waste is covered and allowed to decompose, isolated from the environment for safe disposal; once completely degraded it is safe. Incineration is burning hazardous materials at temperatures high enough to destroy contaminants; heat can be used as steam. Other method: composting / bioremediation / vermicomposting / breakdown by bacteria or microbes.
key_points: Sanitary landfill: waste covered and isolated, allowed to decompose safely
Incineration: burning waste at very high temperature to destroy contaminants
Another eco-friendly method: composting / vermicomposting / bioremediation
marking_schemes.model_answer: In a sanitary landfill, waste is spread, compacted and covered with soil in a site isolated from the environment, where it decomposes safely. Incineration is the burning of waste at very high temperatures to destroy contaminants; the heat can be used to produce steam. Biodegradable waste can also be disposed of by composting or vermicomposting.
common_errors: Did not include 'at a very high temperature' for incineration
Could not distinguish open and sanitary landfills
Wrote recycling for biodegradable waste

marking_schemes.question_text: What is terracing? Where is it practiced? State three advantages of terracing.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Fields are cut at right angles to the slope and agriculture is carried out on the flat surfaces, to prevent soil erosion. Practised in hilly regions, slopes and mountains (step farming). Advantages: reduces soil erosion / minimises landslides / reduces runoff / reduces wastage of irrigation water / reduces sedimentation / increases water holding / prevents loss of nutrients / more area for crops. (Any three)
key_points: Terracing: cutting steps (flat fields) across the slope for farming
Practised in hilly / mountainous regions
Three advantages: reduces soil erosion; reduces runoff; minimises landslides; saves irrigation water; retains nutrients
marking_schemes.model_answer: Terracing is cutting a hill slope into a series of flat steps at right angles to the slope, on which crops are grown. It is practised in hilly and mountainous regions. Advantages: it reduces soil erosion and surface runoff, minimises landslides, and increases the water-holding capacity of the soil.
common_errors: Described terracing as farming on rooftops
Wrote names of countries instead of hilly regions

marking_schemes.question_text: 'Biogas is produced by fermentation of biodegradable wastes.' Mention any three advantages and any two disadvantages of using biogas.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantages: low cost, eco-friendly, non-polluting / raw material easily available in rural areas / reduces dependence on fossil fuels and firewood / converts waste into useful product / high calorific value / gives rich organic manure / smokeless / reduces deforestation. Disadvantages: not feasible everywhere, especially in cities / difficult to improve efficiency / impurities corrode engine parts / not economical at large scale / needs space / foul smell / transport problems / high installation cost / large volume of raw material.
key_points: Three advantages: cheap and non-polluting; easily available raw material; reduces use of firewood; high calorific value; slurry gives organic manure
Two disadvantages: not feasible in urban areas; needs space; high installation cost; foul smell; large raw material required
marking_schemes.model_answer: Advantages: biogas is a cheap, smokeless and non-polluting fuel; its raw material is easily available in rural areas, which reduces the use of firewood; and the leftover slurry is a rich organic manure. Disadvantages: it is not feasible in urban areas as it needs a lot of space, and the plant's installation cost is high.
common_errors: Confused biogas with biomass
Could not write the disadvantages

marking_schemes.question_text: What are the aims of Integrated Pest Management (IPM)? Write three advantages of IPM.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Aims: balanced ecosystem / avoid crop loss / healthy environment / minimise adverse effects of pesticides / high-quality produce at minimal cost / promote biodiversity / reduce dependence on synthetic pesticides. (Any two) Advantages: effective and environmentally sensitive / economical with least hazard / applicable to agricultural and non-agricultural settings / reduced chance of pest resistance / reduced pesticide use through a variety of control options. (Any three)
key_points: Two aims: avoid crop loss from pests; minimise harmful effects of pesticides; maintain a balanced ecosystem; quality produce at low cost
Three advantages: environmentally sensitive; economical and least hazardous; less pest resistance; reduced pesticide use; usable in many settings
marking_schemes.model_answer: Aims of IPM: to avoid crop losses caused by pests, and to keep the harmful effects of pesticides to a minimum while maintaining a balanced ecosystem. Advantages: it is an effective and environmentally sensitive approach; it reduces the chance of pests developing resistance; and it reduces pesticide use by combining biological, physical and cultural controls.
common_errors: Confused aims with advantages
Wrote the same points for both

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between ex-situ and in-situ conservation. Give one example of in-situ conservation. Write any two advantages of in-situ conservation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: In-situ: in the natural habitat / no special care units / protects habitat and many species / moderate cost / more sustainable / no special breeding skills. Ex-situ: outside natural habitat / special care units / conserves threatened species / high cost / special breeding skills. Examples: sanctuaries, national parks, biosphere reserves. Advantages: protects natural habitats / maintains viable numbers / legislation / research and education / natural reproduction and traits / evolution continues / tourism. (Any two)
key_points: Difference: in-situ in the natural habitat vs ex-situ outside it (zoos, gardens, seed banks)
Example of in-situ: national park / sanctuary / biosphere reserve
Two advantages of in-situ: natural habitat protected; species keep natural traits and breed naturally; many species conserved together; lower cost
marking_schemes.model_answer: In-situ conservation protects organisms in their natural habitat, while ex-situ conservation protects them outside their natural habitat in places such as zoos and botanical gardens under special care. Example of in-situ: a national park such as Jim Corbett. Advantages: the whole natural habitat and many species are protected together, and animals breed naturally and keep their natural traits.
common_errors: Wrote incompatible points of difference
Wrote only definitions

marking_schemes.question_text: List any two ecological impacts of Urbanisation. What three measures can be adopted to strengthen rural-urban linkage?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ecological impacts: pollutants from factories / waste and disease / urban sprawl destroys habitats / loss of farmland, wetlands, grazing land / altered local climate / loss of biodiversity and resources. (Any two) Linkage: flow of farm produce to urban markets / flow of market information / flow of farm technology / rural development and microfinance schemes / agro-based industry / agro and village tourism / more village markets. (Any three)
key_points: Two ecological impacts: habitat loss from urban sprawl; loss of farmland and wetlands; loss of biodiversity; pollution; altered local climate
Three linkage measures: flow of produce to urban markets; flow of information and technology; agro-based industries; rural development and microfinance; agro-tourism
marking_schemes.model_answer: Urbanisation destroys natural habitats as cities sprawl, and it converts fertile farmland and wetlands into built-up land. Rural-urban linkage can be strengthened by improving the flow of farm produce from villages to urban markets, sharing market information and new farming technology with farmers, and setting up agro-based industries in rural areas.
common_errors: Wrote social, cultural and economic impacts instead of ecological ones
Could not write measures for rural-urban linkage

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the expanded form of GMO. Write two benefits and two problems associated with these organisms.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Genetically Modified Organisms. Benefits: disease, flood and drought resistant crops / nutritious food / more yield / lower cost of food and drugs / pest resistance / better quality / food security. Problems: altered metabolism / new allergens / ecological imbalance / super pests and weeds / unknown safety / small farmers suffer / gene transfer to conventional varieties / loss of original germplasm.
key_points: Genetically Modified Organism
Two benefits: pest and disease resistance; higher yield; more nutritious food; food security
Two problems: allergens; unknown long-term safety; superweeds and pests; gene transfer; harms small farmers
marking_schemes.model_answer: GMO stands for Genetically Modified Organism. Benefits: GM crops can be pest and drought resistant, and they give higher yields of more nutritious food. Problems: GM food may introduce new allergens, and genes may transfer to conventional varieties, causing loss of original germplasm.
common_errors: Could not write the expanded form
Did not explain the benefits and problems

marking_schemes.question_text: What is Community Forestry? State two objectives of community forestry. How does this forestry benefit the community?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Raising of trees on community land / social area / conservation of forest with the help of the community. Benefits and objectives: government provides seeds, seedlings and fertilisers; communities manage the plantations; food and fodder; fuel wood; manure; recreation; the entire community benefits; the community takes responsibility for protecting trees.
key_points: Definition: raising trees on community land with the participation of local people
Objectives and benefits: food, fodder, fuel wood and manure for the community; community manages and protects the trees; recreational needs
marking_schemes.model_answer: Community forestry is the raising of trees on community land with the participation of the local people. Its objectives are to meet the community's needs for fuel wood, fodder and food, and to make the community responsible for protecting the trees. It benefits the community by supplying fuel, fodder, manure and recreational spaces, while the government provides seeds and seedlings.
common_errors: Defined community forestry incorrectly
Confused objectives with advantages

marking_schemes.question_text: What is GEF? Explain any two areas of global environmental issues which is addressed by GEF.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: GEF (Global Environmental Facility) is a partnership for international cooperation. It focuses on: biodiversity, climate change, chemicals, international waters, land degradation, sustainable forest management, ozone depletion.
key_points: GEF = Global Environmental Facility, a partnership for international cooperation (funding)
Two areas explained: biodiversity; climate change; chemicals; international waters; land degradation; forest management; ozone depletion
marking_schemes.model_answer: GEF is the Global Environmental Facility, an international partnership that funds projects on global environmental problems. Two areas it addresses: climate change, by funding projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions; and biodiversity, by supporting the conservation of ecosystems and species.
common_errors: Could not give the expanded form of GEF

marking_schemes.question_text: Suggest five methods by which we can reduce cutting of trees or combat deforestation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reforestation and afforestation / energy plantation / materials other than wood / recycling wood and paper / changing consumption patterns / less wood for paper / strict laws / managing forest grazing / ban firewood use / less wooden furniture / social, agro and community forestry / ban jhumming / Van Mahotsav / silviculture. (Any five)
key_points: Any five methods: afforestation and reforestation; energy plantations; using alternatives to wood; recycling paper and timber; strict forest laws; social / agro / community forestry; banning slash-and-burn
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Afforestation and reforestation. 2. Energy plantations to supply fuel wood. 3. Using materials other than wood and recycling timber and paper. 4. Strict laws for the conservation of forests. 5. Promoting social, agro and community forestry.
common_errors: Wrote impacts of deforestation instead of methods
Repeated similar methods

marking_schemes.question_text: Read the following paragraph and answer the following questions. Counter urbanization is a demographic and social process. Of late urbanization process in India is witnessing counter–urbanization in its life cycle. The counter-urbanization increases urbanism in physically rural areas. The growth in information technology, increase in car ownership over the last 40 years, more mobility, new business parks on the edge of cities, more people tend to move when they retire and so on are factors responsible for counter urbanization. (a) Mention any two causes associated with Counter Urbanization as given in the paragraph. (b) Write two more causes, other than the ones mentioned here, which you think lead people to return to rural areas. (c) What changes will be observed in rural areas as an effect of counter-urbanization?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Growth in information technology / increase in car ownership / more mobility / new business parks on the edge of cities. (b) High land value / high local taxes / cheap land in rural areas / rural development / better transport and communication / congestion and pollution in cities / clean surroundings / new jobs and businesses in villages / better amenities. (c) Changes in demography / loss of original character / change in layout / higher land prices / changes in economy / less public transport use / traffic and pollution in rural areas.
key_points: (a) Two causes from the passage: IT growth; car ownership; mobility; business parks
(b) Two other causes: high land prices and taxes in cities; congestion and pollution in cities; cheap land and clean surroundings in villages; better rural amenities and transport
(c) Effects: change in demography; loss of original character; higher land prices; more traffic and pollution in rural areas
marking_schemes.model_answer: (a) Growth in information technology and increase in car ownership. (b) High land prices and congestion and pollution in cities, and cheaper land with cleaner surroundings in villages. (c) The rural population structure changes, land prices rise, traffic and pollution increase, and villages lose their original character.
common_errors: Could not identify causes given in the passage
Repeated points
Could not explain demographic change in rural areas
